The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; opens 2G only)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-017</td> <td>CI scope</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-018</td> <td>Per-backend <code>power_w</code> definition and rail policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-019</td> <td>Mock adapters use simulated time via an injectable clock</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-020</td> <td>CLI binds <code>FakeClock</code> for all-mock runs, <code>SystemClock</code> otherwise</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-021</td> <td>Controller flushes <code>events.jsonl</code> before the reduce stage</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-022</td> <td>Auto-generated run-ID suffix is config-hash-derived, not random</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-023</td> <td>Per-item phase status lives solely in the exit checklists</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-024</td> <td>Adapters receive a <code>RunContext</code>, not piecemeal parameters</td> <td>accepted; implemented (2N.1, 2026-07-06)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-025</td> <td>One shared bundle read layer for reducer, report, validation, and aggregation</td> <td>accepted; implemented (2N.8, 2026-07-06)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-026</td> <td>Measured window is bounded by sampling-active marker events</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-027</td> <td>Per-rail rows must share per-sample timestamps; misalignment is a structured failure</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-028</td> <td><code>reduce</code> verb rewrites <code>summary_metrics.json</code> in place (the one sanctioned post-finalize mutation)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-029</td> <td>Config schema declares nullable optionals; serialization (and config hashes) unchanged</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-030</td> <td><code>validate-bundle</code> stays structural by default; <code>--strict</code> adds raw-evidence checks</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-031</td> <td>Multi-model council review; PR convention for multi-commit sessions (merge authority amended by C-010); D-023 extension + end-of-session consistency sweep</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-032</td> <td><code>phase_energy_j</code> is gross-only in summary v0.1</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-033</td> <td>Prompt-content provenance is recorded per run bundle</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-034</td> <td>Slice 2O owns the workload program after 2M and 3.0.1; implementation lane reopened by D-042</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-035</td> <td>Replay claims require fresh-process (subprocess-per-stage) isolation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-036</td> <td>Spike verdict codes derive from measured data, never hardcoded</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-037</td> <td>Claims ladder (L0-L4) binds reader-facing claim language from 2M onward</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-038</td> <td>Analysis plans bind L2/L3 claims to pre-registered comparison rows</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-039</td> <td>Workload program v2: substrate first, identification before scale; pre-Window-A allowlist superseded by D-041/D-042</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-040</td> <td>Suite architecture v2: generic suite mechanism, bundle-level replication</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-041</td> <td>Benchmark interop via frozen-subset imports and marker-shim energy layer; operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

docs/paper/draft-v1.md:141:Comparisons use the ABBA blocks defined in Section 4. Conditions A and B are measured in the order A, B, B, A, with ordinary cooldown between members. Averaging the two outer A observations and the two inner B observations cancels a linear time trend within the block to first order. For null-floor calibration, A and B are aliases of the same configuration and payload, so any nonzero block difference is a false comparative effect. For scientific contrasts, the A and B definitions are frozen in advance, and the contrast is computed within each block before blocks are aggregated. ABBA reduces common drift; it does not replace the measured whole-window drift allowance.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:149:Custody — the requirement that every claim trace back to tamper-evident evidence — continues after collection. The immutable corpus is backed up before extraction. The extractor re-authenticates member hashes, required files and cross-file consistency, calibration identity, environment admission, complete campaign membership, cooldown evidence, phase metric identity, and the whole-window drift allowance. It excludes or refuses a cell according to the frozen rules; missing uncertainty never becomes zero. The present boundary is narrower than an independently reusable floor file: a claim-bearing floor must be produced by protocol-controlled extraction and consumed by analysis in one controlled session run and verified by the experimenters. A standalone floor or result artifact is not independently sufficient to authorize a claim.

     5	it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository

     9	  gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of

    12	  volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.

    14	  (D-078 phase 0), the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules
    15	  (D-078 clause 10; council C-045), and the first floor artifact minted
    16	  on 2026-07-30. D-110 has since made that artifact
    17	  **NON-CLAIM-BEARING** until it is re-derived under the repaired
    18	  calibration selector and reminted. A second instrument calibration
    19	  (the 7B model) passed overnight on 2026-07-29, but its mint is blocked
    20	  on the same repair chain.
    21	  The pre-registered head-to-head model comparison **collected and
    22	  passed overnight on 2026-07-30→31** (40 paired measurements, every
    23	  collection-quality gate green). Its result remains a preliminary
    24	  diagnostic, not a gated claim; D-110 blocks formal consumption until the
    25	  calibration repair and remint chain is complete. As of 2026-07-30 the
    26	  project's framing is **metrology-centric** (advisor-ratified): the measurement
    27	  instrument itself is the product, and model comparisons serve as
    28	  demonstration studies of what it can resolve. The first two nights of
    29	  the dedicated metrology campaign ran on 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-01:
    30	  the linearity data set is complete (40 of 40 runs), two of the three
    31	  planned "measure nothing and confirm the instrument reads zero"
    32	  rungs are complete, and the additivity data set stands at 23 of 24
    33	  runs from the second night's single collection root, with 21 of 24
    34	  corroborating runs from the first night. The measurements themselves are collected, verified, and
    35	  safely backed up. The automated end-of-night quality verdict for both
    36	  nights, however, came back FAILED — not because the data is bad, but
    37	  because these were the first nights that ended early under the
    38	  campaign's own safety rules (a run is abandoned after three
    39	  environmental interruptions), and the verdict software had never
    40	  before evaluated a night with that shape. That question has now been adjudicated (decisions D-100 and D-106):
    41	  the first night's data cannot be promoted — an end-of-night

    43	  collection-time error — while the second night's
    44	  re-evaluation was actually attempted on 2026-08-03 after every
    45	  required repair landed — and the software refused, correctly: one
    46	  measured run from that night has a genuinely unresolvable internal
    47	  clock alignment, and the fail-closed design will not certify a night
    48	  containing it. A judge-style review confirmed the refusal was the

   678	## Experiment Plan
   679	
   680	**Homogeneous baselines (Phase 2).** Per target and model: a workload
   681	matrix spanning prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, and balanced profiles
   682	(prompt 128-4096 tokens x decode 64-512), n=5, producing energy/token and
   683	energy/request with intervals - and reproducing the qualitative
   684	prefill/decode power asymmetry that motivates disaggregation.
   685	
   686	**Disaggregation (Phase 3), feasibility-first.** KV-cache portability is
   687	the project's central technical risk, so the phase is a ladder where each
   688	rung is publishable even if the next fails:
   689	
   690	1. *Synthetic transfer microbenchmark* (guaranteed): move KV-sized
   691	   payloads between nodes with both-end power sampling - transfer energy
   692	   and time vs payload size vs link speed, independent of any LLM
   693	   runtime's cooperation.
   694	2. *Offline replay* (primary): persist the prompt cache on the prefill
   695	   node, transfer the file, resume decode on the decode node - same
   696	   pinned runtime on both ends. Per-runtime feasibility spikes (mlx-lm,
   697	   llama.cpp including cross-machine portability, vLLM time-boxed) run
   698	   before any borrowed-hardware scheduling.
   699	3. *Live split* (stretch): streamed KV during the run; explicitly
   700	   droppable without harming the study.
   701	
   702	Payload sizes are analytically predictable (2 x layers x kv_heads x
   703	head_dim x 2 bytes per token, fp16), which drives experiment design - for
   704	a 2048-token prompt: a 1.5B-class model ~56 MiB (~0.5 s at 1GbE), an
   705	8B-class model ~256 MiB (~2.3 s at 1GbE). At 1GbE, mid-size-model
   706	transfer time is the same order as prefill time on weaker devices -
   707	exactly the regime where an energy crossover can exist; the sweep spans
   708	prompt lengths and link speeds accordingly.
   709	
   710	**Analysis (Phase 4).** Aggregation over validated bundles with an
   711	exclusion log (no silent data drops); a deterministic figure pipeline
   712	(every report figure regenerates from a script); a claims-to-evidence
   713	index (every quantitative claim traces to figure -> script -> raw
   714	bundles); a sensitivity audit checking that headline effects exceed their
   715	confidence intervals.

    13	
    14	JouleWise is an extensible measurement harness for energy-wise LLM inference
    15	across heterogeneous local hardware. The benchmark layered on that harness is
    16	the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. The name is a
    17	deliberate nod to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement as the spine,
    18	split inference as the first major research application.
    19	
    20	The harness is designed around three stable ideas:
    21	
    22	- Typed experiment configs define what should run.
    23	- Runtime and telemetry adapters define how each hardware target is exercised
    24	  and measured.
    25	- Run bundles preserve raw traces, events, metadata, logs, and summary metrics
    26	  for later audit and analysis.
    27	
    28	**Status:** research prototype. The Mac (Apple M3 Max) measurement harness has
    29	completed its instrument repair (D-078 phase 0) and the repaired path has
    30	collected 229 strict members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those
    31	windows are non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence, not
    32	published floors. The SCREEN+BUDGET rules are ratified and merged
    33	(D-078 clause 10; council C-045):
    34	they screen gross and idle-subtracted energy separately, retain a nonzero
    35	drift allowance for each family, require a fresh 24-hour bound, reject
    36	fallback-clock members from floor cells, and bar mock evidence from claims.
    37	Five prospective quiet-machine windows have since passed under those rules
    38	(C, D, a10, the 7B floor window, and the contrast window). The first floor
    39	artifact was minted on 2026-07-30, but D-110 has since made that mint
    40	**NON-CLAIM-BEARING until it is re-derived under the repaired calibration
    41	selector**. The Splitwise head-to-head contrast (1.5B vs 7B decode) has been
    42	collected and passed its collection and whole-window verdict gates; its
    43	bookkeeping machinery and generalized mint tooling are mainline, but D-110
    44	blocks claim use and the next floor mint until the ruled repair and remint
    45	conditions are satisfied. The a8 re-verdict path is closed. The
    46	project's framing is now metrology-centric (D-091): the measurement
    47	instrument itself is the product, and model comparisons are demonstrations
    48	of what it can resolve.
    49	
    50	The post-audit architectural verdicts remain deliberately bounded: AXI-SB is
    51	`supported` for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped
    52	observability, while AXI-SC is `unsupported_for_joulewise` on the pinned
    53	runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution
    54	surface is absent. Neither is energy evidence. This summary does not select
    55	work: the generated state-kernel regions in `RUN_STATE.md` and `TASK_QUEUE.md`
    56	own live gates and next-task state. Quiet-machine execution still requires the
    57	lead-controlled hardware lane with Ed. The verified end-user quickstart remains
    58	a Phase 5 deliverable.
    59

    67	## Current Repository View — 30-second read
    68	
    69	**The repaired measurement path has produced its first floor artifact, but
    70	that artifact is not currently claim-bearing.** The D-078 phase-0 repair
    71	fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22; the drift-screen
    72	rules merged on 2026-07-25; the first fully clean measurement windows
    73	passed on 2026-07-25/26, and on 2026-07-30 the project minted its first
    74	floor artifact from them. D-110 later made that mint non-claim-bearing
    75	pending governed re-derivation and remint. A second calibration window
    76	(the 7B model) passed overnight on 2026-07-29, surviving two
    77	live contamination events that the admission gates caught and recovered
    78	from per the written playbook. The earlier a5-a8 windows (229 members)
    79	remain non-claim-bearing, instrument-proving evidence.
    80	
    81	**The head-to-head comparison ran on 2026-07-30→31 and passed every
    82	collection and whole-window gate.** Comparing the small (1.5B) and large (7B)
    83	model decoding the same text, the large model used **about 147 J (whole-request, idle-subtracted — a diagnostic view; the registered per-phase comparison metric gives 141.29 J) more energy per response**
    84	— and the run-to-run scatter of that difference across ten paired blocks
    85	was only about **0.24 J**, roughly six hundred times smaller than the
    86	effect. This is the kind of demonstration the metrology framing calls for: a
    87	real effect the instrument resolves with enormous margin, measured under
    88	frozen, pre-registered rules. (Preliminary observation from the raw
    89	per-run summaries. The comparison's bookkeeping schema landed on
    90	2026-08-02, but D-110 blocks formal consumption until the calibration
    91	repair and remint chain is complete.) The same overnight session survived two
    92	background-process intrusions — macOS's own malware scanner — which the
    93	admission gates refused on the spot and the written recovery playbook
    94	turned into a completed window with zero lost science measurements.
    95	
    96	That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and
    97	idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a
    98	nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires
    99	after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock
   100	evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims.
   101	This protocol has now run five times — windows C, D, a10, the 7B floor
   102	window, and the contrast window — each minting its bound inside the
   103	window and collecting three start references, one midpoint reference,
   104	and three end references.
   105	The older 222-bundle floor record below remains visible as a permanently
   106	**VOIDED** historical record, not the current measurement posture.
   107	
   108	AXI-SB remains `supported` for native static-batch runtime feasibility with
   109	request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is
   110	`unsupported_for_joulewise` on the pinned runtime because the required
   111	speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither
   112	verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the
   113	generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.

   146	UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid
   147	bundles with clean source provenance (`runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/`)
   148	cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n,
   149	including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source
   150	provenance gate is closed. **SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a
   151	same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from
   152	the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.**
   153	In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two
   154	different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to
   155	~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the
   156	workload's start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the
   157	wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for short test runs and still a
   158	meaningful hidden uncertainty on longer ones. Those numerical examples are
   159	**VOIDED**, not corrected measurements. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are
   160	intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across
   161	nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply
   162	below this instrument's resolution and will not be claimed — by
   163	design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter's own timestamps,
   164	attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate
   165	end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is
   166	implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer:
   167	`docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md`; technical
   168	record: `docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md`.
   169	
   170	**REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and
   171	signed off.** Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole
   172	measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent
   173	adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last
   174	round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the
   175	instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened
   176	relative to the model's work (the clock-alignment fix, with the
   177	alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every
   178	result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is
   179	genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with,
   180	mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is
   250	  restart rows.

## Counting method

A “catch” is one independently named defect, defect class, or decision-invalidating finding attributed to a layer. I excluded clean verification, duplicated rediscovery, design recommendations without an identified failure, and refuter suppressions/repricings from the catch total. Those suppressions are reported separately.

The log changes granularity over time: some entries say `~20`, `10+`, or `~60`. Accordingly, `≥` is the auditable minimum, not false precision. `U` means severity unstated.

## 2. Spend signals

- Early councils were effectively unmetered: C-005 records five Codex lenses; C-007 records eight read-only sessions, both described as approximately free under the then-current quota doctrine ([C-005 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:451>), [C-007 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:796>)).

- C-028 is the anti-example: **59 Sol sessions, 330.6M tokens, ~17.5 hours, ~$1,050 combined estimated cost**, with a ~$2,300 non-manifest upper bound. Sol produced ~180× the token volume, but Fable was ~3.4× the estimated cost because cache reads dominated ([C-028 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:1627>)).

- The clearest effort-control experiment is C-029→C-030: accidental ULTRA consumed **~118M tokens over 13 invocations**; corrected explicit xhigh consumed **~7.0M over three sessions** while still producing DRA-001 and XSI-1—roughly a 17× aggregate-token reduction ([C-029/C-030](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:1517>)).

- C-034 crossed the arc HARD band: **28 Sol sessions, ~251M tokens**. C-035 then used **~14 sessions, ~71.2M tokens** for three spec pipelines ([C-034/C-035](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:1521>)).

- C-045 used **11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations** for the gauntlet, ~15 for the day, plus four Opus agents totaling roughly **475k tokens**. Its usage feed returned zeros and was explicitly recorded as unavailable, not zero spend ([C-045 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:1824>)).

- C-038 provides the best model-allocation micro-signal: Opus contract lens **164k tokens / 11 min**; Fable adjudication **21k / 108 seconds / zero tool uses**; Sol audit and diagnosis **23 + 17 minutes**. The tiny, pre-assembled Fable judgment consult overturned the lead more cheaply than another retrieval-heavy pass ([C-038 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2056>)).

Expensive, but every layer caught something and the refuter amended all three gates ([C-040 outcome](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2501>)).

- In-window consults appear highly leveraged: one bounded consult protected a **~2.6-hour** window; another cost one session against an **11-hour** runway ([C-039 addenda](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2356>)).

## 3. Zero-yield streaks and drop candidates

There is **no currently eligible automatic drop candidate**.

The old C-006 rule—two zero-catch sessions—was superseded by D-061: three mechanically applicable exposures trigger an expected-loss review, never automatic deletion; safety, final-head, and integration layers are protected.

Observed streaks:

- **CI:** at least three recent green applicable exposures without a unique catch—C-046, C-048, C-049. It is not drop-eligible: CI is a low-token structural merge-ref oracle, and C-022 records the one interaction no other layer could see.

- **Cold Fable instance:** had a temporary zero-unique streak in the C-040 addendum/C-041 gates, where the paired refuter supplied the decisive findings. C-047 reset that streak with three unique catches.

- **Integration review:** C-036 was explicitly zero, but the log does not establish two later mechanically applicable independent integration-review exposures. C-048 used an integration tree as a lead gate, not a separate integration review.

- **Suite-pruning lens:** one zero-yield exposure in C-039 only—insufficient.

- The original generic Opus refuter/verifier was already dropped under the old rule at C-006. That is not evidence against the later **distinct contract + execution refuter pair**, which is one of the highest-yield instruments.

## 4. Recurring lead error classes

Counts below are atomic incidents where the log supports them; `≥` reflects plural or approximate source language.

| Lead-error habit | Count | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Piped suite exit status masking | **3** | First `tail` masking in C-038, recurrence in C-047, explicitly called the **third occurrence** in C-048. |
| Other exit-0/non-result confusion | **2 additional** | C-037 stale-lock exit-0 wart; C-038 wrapper returned zero for a read-only session that did no work. |
| Stale `RUN_STATE` claims | **4 atomic claims across 3 entries** | C-007 general staleness; C-027 dual next-action; C-048’s two stale active claims. |
| Council/index-row drift | **≥5 row defects across 4 entries** | Missing C-005/C-006 rows in C-007; missing C-018 row in C-019; duplicate/mismatched D-064 rows in C-033; C-046 required retrospective reconstruction. |
| Packet/evidence/dictation hygiene | **≥19 atomic errors across 5 entries** | Five dictated-entry errors in C-045; four C-038 verification discrepancies; two C-040-addendum packet failures; four repeated packet-hygiene findings in C-041; four packet/counter errors in C-042. |
| Live-tree/two-writer violations | **3** | Same-main-tree bookkeeping/fix collision in C-025; installed-runner edit during a live run in C-028; lead bench edit during enforced scope in C-043. |
| Scope/interface launch mistakes | **11** | Three lead-guessed scope misses in C-028; three `WRITE_SCOPE` rc=64 launches in C-029; three invalid-JSON launches plus one missing sandbox in C-038; one lead stray file in C-037. |

The clearest “habit has not stuck” signals are exit-status discipline, packet factual hygiene, state/index bookkeeping, scope-launch preparation, and exclusive tree ownership. Each recurred after an explicit corrective doctrine had already been recorded.

## 5. Recommendations ranked by expected catch-per-token

1. **Install one mechanical lead-closeout preflight.** Highest expected return because it spends almost no model tokens and attacks the densest recurring classes. It should refuse completion unless: suite execution is unpiped with its own summary; delegated envelopes report actual completion; `RUN_STATE` active claims and council index rows reconcile; no second writer owns the tree; quoted gate clauses/flags are complete; and declared scope parses before launch. The named-failure bar is amply met by the counts above.

2. **Keep fresh delta re-audit after every fix, but default it to bounded HIGH with changed-path/reachability probes.** It produced **57 catches, including 17 stated blockers**. C-048 showed HIGH still found a live blocker on a 127-line mostly-test change, while C-029→C-030 demonstrates the enormous token penalty of accidental high effort. Escalate only on repeated signature or decision ambiguity.

3. **Retain the distinct contract + execution refuter pair only for blocker/cold-gate findings, with runnable probes required.** It supplied **40 catches plus ≥20 suppressions/repricings**, and repeatedly outperformed same-family agreement. C-045 showed HIGH refuters were sufficient; C-040/C-041 showed the pairing—not an additional homogeneous reviewer—is what corrected adjudicator/cold-instance convergence. Batch should-fixes and nits without refuters.

Bottom line: spend less on broad homogeneous audit volume and more on three narrow instruments—mechanical lead hygiene, fresh post-fix re-audit, and probe-bearing cross-model refutation. CI stays as cheap structural insurance, not as a defect-discovery layer.

## Counting method

A “catch” is one independently named defect, defect class, or decision-invalidating finding attributed to a layer. I excluded clean verification, duplicated rediscovery, design recommendations without an identified failure, and refuter suppressions/repricings from the catch total. Those suppressions are reported separately.

The log changes granularity over time: some entries say `~20`, `10+`, or `~60`. Accordingly, `≥` is the auditable minimum, not false precision. `U` means severity unstated.

## 3. Zero-yield streaks and drop candidates

There is **no currently eligible automatic drop candidate**.

The old C-006 rule—two zero-catch sessions—was superseded by D-061: three mechanically applicable exposures trigger an expected-loss review, never automatic deletion; safety, final-head, and integration layers are protected.

Observed streaks:

- **CI:** at least three recent green applicable exposures without a unique catch—C-046, C-048, C-049. It is not drop-eligible: CI is a low-token structural merge-ref oracle, and C-022 records the one interaction no other layer could see.

- **Cold Fable instance:** had a temporary zero-unique streak in the C-040 addendum/C-041 gates, where the paired refuter supplied the decisive findings. C-047 reset that streak with three unique catches.

- **Integration review:** C-036 was explicitly zero, but the log does not establish two later mechanically applicable independent integration-review exposures. C-048 used an integration tree as a lead gate, not a separate integration review.

- **Suite-pruning lens:** one zero-yield exposure in C-039 only—insufficient.

- The original generic Opus refuter/verifier was already dropped under the old rule at C-006. That is not evidence against the later **distinct contract + execution refuter pair**, which is one of the highest-yield instruments.
