## 5. Recommendations ranked by expected catch-per-token

1. **Install one mechanical lead-closeout preflight.** Highest expected return because it spends almost no model tokens and attacks the densest recurring classes. It should refuse completion unless: suite execution is unpiped with its own summary; delegated envelopes report actual completion; `RUN_STATE` active claims and council index rows reconcile; no second writer owns the tree; quoted gate clauses/flags are complete; and declared scope parses before launch. The named-failure bar is amply met by the counts above.

2. **Keep fresh delta re-audit after every fix, but default it to bounded HIGH with changed-path/reachability probes.** It produced **57 catches, including 17 stated blockers**. C-048 showed HIGH still found a live blocker on a 127-line mostly-test change, while C-029→C-030 demonstrates the enormous token penalty of accidental high effort. Escalate only on repeated signature or decision ambiguity.

3. **Retain the distinct contract + execution refuter pair only for blocker/cold-gate findings, with runnable probes required.** It supplied **40 catches plus ≥20 suppressions/repricings**, and repeatedly outperformed same-family agreement. C-045 showed HIGH refuters were sufficient; C-040/C-041 showed the pairing—not an additional homogeneous reviewer—is what corrected adjudicator/cold-instance convergence. Batch should-fixes and nits without refuters.

Bottom line: spend less on broad homogeneous audit volume and more on three narrow instruments—mechanical lead hygiene, fresh post-fix re-audit, and probe-bearing cross-model refutation. CI stays as cheap structural insurance, not as a defect-discovery layer.

## Verdict

The fast-mode fan-out was a protocol violation, not an allowed “non-governed mode.”

The bridge contract covers Claude–Codex collaboration generally and says every delegated prompt must begin with `BRIDGE_TASK_V1` ([§1, lines 28–53](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:28)); autonomous calls require the full header even when read-only ([§1, lines 99–100](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:99)). The routing table sends autonomous work to audited CLI; it does not define an ungoverned or fast-tier exception ([§4, lines 225–238](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:225)).

The only audited-CLI exception is from the two-line trailer when a valid `claude-codex-report/v1` body exists; it does not waive the prompt header ([§2, lines 138–145](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:138)). Section 9’s statement that enforcement exists only where adapters validate it is a limitation, not an opt-out ([§9, lines 781–785](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:781)).

### Confirmed bypasses

1. **Bare fast-mode prompts and noncompliant returns.**  
   The representative proposal transcript starts directly with “PAPER-PROPOSAL DEVELOPMENT SESSION,” not a bridge header ([proposal lines 1–17](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-attention-variant-energy.md:1)), and ends in ordinary prose rather than either accepted return form ([lines 5206–5212](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-attention-variant-energy.md:5206)). The same is true of the two xhigh syntheses ([example lines 12–24](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:12)). Contract §2 explicitly says missing or malformed required envelopes cannot be interpreted as success ([lines 174–183](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:174)).

2. **Implementation/audit prompts used an older ad hoc contract.**  
   U1 begins with only `WRITE_SCOPE: [...]`, omitting `TASK_SHAPE`, `GENRE`, `BASE_HEAD`, baseline manifest/digest, acceptance, verification, and output protocol ([U1 lines 1–12](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-CONTRACT.md:1)). The audit likewise begins bare ([U1 audit lines 14–21](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-AUDIT-CONTRACT.md:14)). This fails §1 and the mandatory pre-write baseline rule in §7 ([lines 543–573](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:543)), even if `codex-run-v3` separately performed its older post-hoc scope check.

3. **“Fast mode” was treated as governance selection.**  
   The ratification says standard-tier `codex-run-v3` is used when scope enforcement matters and fast mode for all read-only/ideation work ([lines 31–39](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-plan-freeze/RATIFICATION.md:31)). That is the conceptual error: service tier affects latency/credits, not whether headers, output validation, provenance, or status semantics apply. The per-call directive itself is recorded only in live state ([RUN_STATE lines 427–436](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:427)).

4. **The completed C-049 working session still lacks its required run report.**  
   Orchestration requires one run report per working session and describes it as the session record ([lines 84–90](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:84), [artifact table lines 146–155](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:146)); M0 repeats that requirement ([lines 74–78](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/agent_playbook.md:74)). C-049 instead identifies scattered traces and `RUN_STATE` blocks as its full record ([C-049 lines 2798–2808](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2798)); no August 5/6 run report exists.

5. **Portfolio consumption is not auditable at the prescribed invocation level.**  
   Orchestration requires model, wrapper, session ID, prompt hash/path, output path, status, consumer, disposition, and commit/PR for each substantial invocation ([lines 180–187](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:180)). The adjudication records “24 Sol + 24 Opus + two syntheses” ([lines 3–8](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/ADJUDICATION.md:3)), but the tracked corpus has no invocation-to-artifact/consumer/disposition manifest, especially for the Opus reviews. It also lacks the complete high-impact-council scorecard required by orchestration ([lines 191–205](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:191)). Because today’s session remains live, this is still remediable, but it is current compliance debt.

I did not classify the unfinished U1/U3 gauntlets or the absent end-of-session sweep as violations: `RUN_STATE` explicitly marks the session and those units in flight.

## Routine practice missing from prescriptive docs

- **Opus counter-reviewer/lieutenant layer.** The council’s standing-role text still says the Opus tier was dropped ([lines 23–33](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:23)), while later practice made Opus the primary lieutenant ([C-038 lines 1891–1904](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:1891)) and today used 24 Opus referees. No named process doc defines its applicability, independence, authority ceiling, or yield/sunset rule.

- **Proposal factory.** The `24 proposal → 24 paired referee → two opposing-prior syntheses → magistrate adjudication` topology is now relied upon for paper strategy, but no process document specifies its packet, provenance, scoring, duplication handling, or stopping rule.

- **Per-call fast-tier opt-in.** Live state records `CODEX_SERVICE_TIER=fast`, never standing-default ([RUN_STATE lines 431–436](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:431)); neither `CLAUDE.md` nor the bridge contract records that doctrine.

- **Tracked-poll/watcher lifecycle.** Five wake failures established the mandatory status-file/PID/deadline pattern ([run report lines 119–125](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/run_reports/2026-07-28-floor-mint-implementation.md:119)), and stale `RUNNING` has already survived a dead job ([council lines 2197–2203](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2197)). The contract defines thread states ([§5, lines 332–350](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:332)) but never maps them to wrapper `.status` files, PID liveness, stale-state recovery, or consumption.

- **Same-signature escalation/cold-gate rule.** C-049 treats two repeated defect signatures as the trigger for escalation and runs every fix through delta re-audit ([lines 2810–2823](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:2810)); today’s U1 delta repeats that stop condition ([lines 81–89](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-DELTA-VERDICT.md:81)). No named prescriptive document defines “rule 11,” the signature counter, gate composition, or termination semantics.

## Stale or misleading claims

- `docs/council_log.md` still names gpt-5.5 as the standing Codex peer and says Opus was dropped, while today’s transcripts identify `gpt-5.6-sol` and Opus is routine.
- `RUN_STATE`’s “Current Verification” still calls 2,418 tests at an August 2 head current ([lines 2503–2508](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:2503)); today’s U1 audit ran 2,682 ([lines 40678–40694](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-u-units/U1-AUDIT-EXEC.md:40678)).
- The same state document records Codex CLI 0.144.0 ([lines 2691–2696](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:2691)); today’s raw transcripts show 0.146.1.
- M0 directs readers to a `RUN_STATE.md` “What Is Next” section that does not exist ([playbook lines 52–56](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/agent_playbook.md:52)). Its “Current Project Status” is materially older than the August 7 live block.
- The live generated queue still describes `MET-WINDOW-C-01` and a T3-dependent `QUIET-GUARD-01`; the plan-freeze memo itself flags those rows as superseded ([memo lines 180–182](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-d117-plan-freeze/DESIGN-MEMO.md:180)). Historical T3 blocks are correctly labelled and explicitly superseded ([RUN_STATE lines 522–533](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/RUN_STATE.md:522)); the dangerous remnant is the live projection, not the retained history.
- The `codex-run-v3` version claim in `CLAUDE.md` is not stale: v3 is still installed and used for scoped implementation. What is stale is the claim’s completeness—`scripts/codex-bridge` is now the separate fast route, but its service-tier and governance relationship are undocumented ([CLAUDE lines 54–69](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/CLAUDE.md:54)).

## Top five amendments by future-session risk

1. **Fail-close every Claude→Sol launcher on bridge compliance.** Auto-inject or validate the §1 header; reject outputs lacking either a valid full report or required trailer. State explicitly that `service_tier=fast` never changes governance.

2. **Repair the authoritative intake path.** Update M0’s section names, regenerate the kernel projections for D-117, remove live T3 gates, and make current verification/version facts generated or explicitly dated.

3. **Specify one lifecycle state machine.** Map wrapper `RUNNING/OK/FAILED`, bridge `pending/active/waiting_lead/complete`, PID liveness, poll deadlines, stale-state recovery, and manifest consumption. A stale `RUNNING` file must never establish in-flight work.

4. **Ratify the actual review topology.** Add Opus contract counter-review, magistrate adjudication, paired cold gates, delta re-audits, and same-signature escalation—with applicability predicates, authority limits, marginal budget, and sunset criteria required by orchestration’s process-innovation rule ([lines 238–248](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/orchestration.md:238)).

5. **Document the proposal-factory recipe and evidence closure.** Require per-call provenance, paired-review mapping, opposing-prior synthesis, duplication analysis, council scorecard, spend snapshot, and final `consumed_by`/disposition rows before adjudication is called binding.

No files were written. Final inspection showed only a concurrently created untracked `docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-meta-sweeps/` directory; I did not touch it.

5932:## 3. Zero-yield streaks and drop candidates
5936:The old C-006 rule—two zero-catch sessions—was superseded by D-061: three mechanically applicable exposures trigger an expected-loss review, never automatic deletion; safety, final-head, and integration layers are protected.
5940:- **CI:** at least three recent green applicable exposures without a unique catch—C-046, C-048, C-049. It is not drop-eligible: CI is a low-token structural merge-ref oracle, and C-022 records the one interaction no other layer could see.
5942:- **Cold Fable instance:** had a temporary zero-unique streak in the C-040 addendum/C-041 gates, where the paired refuter supplied the decisive findings. C-047 reset that streak with three unique catches.
5944:- **Integration review:** C-036 was explicitly zero, but the log does not establish two later mechanically applicable independent integration-review exposures. C-048 used an integration tree as a lead gate, not a separate integration review.
5946:- **Suite-pruning lens:** one zero-yield exposure in C-039 only—insufficient.
5948:- The original generic Opus refuter/verifier was already dropped under the old rule at C-006. That is not evidence against the later **distinct contract + execution refuter pair**, which is one of the highest-yield instruments.

5969:## 5. Recommendations ranked by expected catch-per-token
5971:1. **Install one mechanical lead-closeout preflight.** Highest expected return because it spends almost no model tokens and attacks the densest recurring classes. It should refuse completion unless: suite execution is unpiped with its own summary; delegated envelopes report actual completion; `RUN_STATE` active claims and council index rows reconcile; no second writer owns the tree; quoted gate clauses/flags are complete; and declared scope parses before launch. The named-failure bar is amply met by the counts above.
5973:2. **Keep fresh delta re-audit after every fix, but default it to bounded HIGH with changed-path/reachability probes.** It produced **57 catches, including 17 stated blockers**. C-048 showed HIGH still found a live blocker on a 127-line mostly-test change, while C-029→C-030 demonstrates the enormous token penalty of accidental high effort. Escalate only on repeated signature or decision ambiguity.
5975:3. **Retain the distinct contract + execution refuter pair only for blocker/cold-gate findings, with runnable probes required.** It supplied **40 catches plus ≥20 suppressions/repricings**, and repeatedly outperformed same-family agreement. C-045 showed HIGH refuters were sufficient; C-040/C-041 showed the pairing—not an additional homogeneous reviewer—is what corrected adjudicator/cold-instance convergence. Batch should-fixes and nits without refuters.

6006:## 2. Spend signals
6008:- Early councils were effectively unmetered: C-005 records five Codex lenses; C-007 records eight read-only sessions, both described as approximately free under the then-current quota doctrine ([C-005 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:451>), [C-007 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:796>)).
6010:- C-028 is the anti-example: **59 Sol sessions, 330.6M tokens, ~17.5 hours, ~$1,050 combined estimated cost**, with a ~$2,300 non-manifest upper bound. Sol produced ~180× the token volume, but Fable was ~3.4× the estimated cost because cache reads dominated ([C-028 spend](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/council_log.md:1627>)).

6024:## 3. Zero-yield streaks and drop candidates
6028:The old C-006 rule—two zero-catch sessions—was superseded by D-061: three mechanically applicable exposures trigger an expected-loss review, never automatic deletion; safety, final-head, and integration layers are protected.
6032:- **CI:** at least three recent green applicable exposures without a unique catch—C-046, C-048, C-049. It is not drop-eligible: CI is a low-token structural merge-ref oracle, and C-022 records the one interaction no other layer could see.
6034:- **Cold Fable instance:** had a temporary zero-unique streak in the C-040 addendum/C-041 gates, where the paired refuter supplied the decisive findings. C-047 reset that streak with three unique catches.
6036:- **Integration review:** C-036 was explicitly zero, but the log does not establish two later mechanically applicable independent integration-review exposures. C-048 used an integration tree as a lead gate, not a separate integration review.
6038:- **Suite-pruning lens:** one zero-yield exposure in C-039 only—insufficient.
6040:- The original generic Opus refuter/verifier was already dropped under the old rule at C-006. That is not evidence against the later **distinct contract + execution refuter pair**, which is one of the highest-yield instruments.

6059:The clearest “habit has not stuck” signals are exit-status discipline, packet factual hygiene, state/index bookkeeping, scope-launch preparation, and exclusive tree ownership. Each recurred after an explicit corrective doctrine had already been recorded.
6061:## 5. Recommendations ranked by expected catch-per-token
6063:1. **Install one mechanical lead-closeout preflight.** Highest expected return because it spends almost no model tokens and attacks the densest recurring classes. It should refuse completion unless: suite execution is unpiped with its own summary; delegated envelopes report actual completion; `RUN_STATE` active claims and council index rows reconcile; no second writer owns the tree; quoted gate clauses/flags are complete; and declared scope parses before launch. The named-failure bar is amply met by the counts above.
6065:2. **Keep fresh delta re-audit after every fix, but default it to bounded HIGH with changed-path/reachability probes.** It produced **57 catches, including 17 stated blockers**. C-048 showed HIGH still found a live blocker on a 127-line mostly-test change, while C-029→C-030 demonstrates the enormous token penalty of accidental high effort. Escalate only on repeated signature or decision ambiguity.
6067:3. **Retain the distinct contract + execution refuter pair only for blocker/cold-gate findings, with runnable probes required.** It supplied **40 catches plus ≥20 suppressions/repricings**, and repeatedly outperformed same-family agreement. C-045 showed HIGH refuters were sufficient; C-040/C-041 showed the pairing—not an additional homogeneous reviewer—is what corrected adjudicator/cold-instance convergence. Batch should-fixes and nits without refuters.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-PROBES.md:1452:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-cross-runtime-contrast.md:7682:JouleWise already has the scientific core of this paper: an in-window pulse-train calibration for phase-boundary attribution; the finding that roughly 30 ms of edge uncertainty across roughly 33 W makes the instrument attribution-limited at about 1 J per phase member; separately enforced floor-clearance and interval-supported-direction gates, producing an effective phase-contrast sizing bar near 5 J; and a fail-closed protocol built around pre-registration, admission checks, ABBA ordering, live brackets, immutable custody, and publishable refusals. The [MVP draft](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-JouleWise/58ce57f7-1ee6-4b35-a1b3-457ccf40dff7/scratchpad/desk/docs/paper/draft-v1.md>) supplies essentially all method, metrology, related-work, and limitations prose. First execute D-117 unchanged: the approximately 3.14 h 1.5B MLX floor window, 3.24 h 7B MLX floor window, and 2.80 h MLX model-size contrast window, with prefill floors riding the first two. Mint those four phase-floor cells and populate the MVP. Then perform a read-only/daytime feasibility stage for llama.cpp: pin one llama.cpp commit and Metal build; derive a GGUF 4-bit artifact and the MLX 4-bit artifact from the same Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct source revision; implement and validate real prefill/decode markers; and run explicitly non-claim pilot comparisons. If the desk gate passes, collect one approximately 3.3 h llama.cpp 7B floor window and one approximately 3.0–3.5 h MLX-versus-llama.cpp ABBA contrast window. Thus the proposal costs **five quiet nights from today—three already required by D-117 plus two new nights**—and perhaps 2–4 weeks of desk engineering. It does not displace or weaken the MVP: if the extension dies, the original paper remains intact.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-PROBES.md:2555:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11456:JouleWise already contains the spine of a strong measurement-methodology paper: a complete-in-structure MVP draft; a 59-pulse, in-window bracket calibration; worst-case phase-edge integration; separately measured repeatability and never-zero drift; two independent claim gates; and a fail-closed, hash-bound protocol whose refusals are retained as evidence. Its central empirical finding is that the M3 Max instrument is attribution-limited: roughly 30 ms of edge uncertainty across a roughly 33 W transition can misassign about 1 J, while ordinary repeatability is nearer 0.3 J. Because the calibrated floor and the contrast’s own interval are separate requirements, practical phase contrasts need roughly 5 J, and repetition cannot average away the boundary term. No current demonstration number is claim-bearing: D-117 therefore requires three fresh prospective windows—1.5B decode floor with a free prefill rider, 7B decode floor with a prefill rider, and a 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast—budgeted at 3.14, 3.24, and 2.80 hours respectively. From today, first finish the two-slot calibration-ledger session, D-102 successor builder, four-cell mint, campaign packs, extraction specifications, and synthetic refusal regression; then collect and mint the two floor windows, collect gamma, and populate the MVP tables. Only afterward should this paper add two compact portability sessions on the desktop rig: one NVML GPU-counter characterization and, if the host exposes a usable package-energy counter, one RAPL characterization. The honest target is therefore **five quiet-device sessions: three already required Mac nights plus two estimated 2–3-hour desktop sessions**. If RAPL capability fails at the desk gate, the paper shrinks to a counter-agnostic framework evaluated on `powermetrics` and NVML, with RAPL described only as a future instantiation—not falsely presented as validated.

Mint the four phase-floor cells, govern the contrast against the two decode floors, and populate the MVP tables. Those three windows contribute the paper’s metrology evidence and Qwen2.5 demonstration; their floors cannot be borrowed for MoE.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:5019:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11456:JouleWise already contains the spine of a strong measurement-methodology paper: a complete-in-structure MVP draft; a 59-pulse, in-window bracket calibration; worst-case phase-edge integration; separately measured repeatability and never-zero drift; two independent claim gates; and a fail-closed, hash-bound protocol whose refusals are retained as evidence. Its central empirical finding is that the M3 Max instrument is attribution-limited: roughly 30 ms of edge uncertainty across a roughly 33 W transition can misassign about 1 J, while ordinary repeatability is nearer 0.3 J. Because the calibrated floor and the contrast’s own interval are separate requirements, practical phase contrasts need roughly 5 J, and repetition cannot average away the boundary term. No current demonstration number is claim-bearing: D-117 therefore requires three fresh prospective windows—1.5B decode floor with a free prefill rider, 7B decode floor with a prefill rider, and a 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast—budgeted at 3.14, 3.24, and 2.80 hours respectively. From today, first finish the two-slot calibration-ledger session, D-102 successor builder, four-cell mint, campaign packs, extraction specifications, and synthetic refusal regression; then collect and mint the two floor windows, collect gamma, and populate the MVP tables. Only afterward should this paper add two compact portability sessions on the desktop rig: one NVML GPU-counter characterization and, if the host exposes a usable package-energy counter, one RAPL characterization. The honest target is therefore **five quiet-device sessions: three already required Mac nights plus two estimated 2–3-hour desktop sessions**. If RAPL capability fails at the desk gate, the paper shrinks to a counter-agnostic framework evaluated on `powermetrics` and NVML, with RAPL described only as a future instantiation—not falsely presented as validated.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-RESULTS_PROSE.md:663:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11199:JouleWise already has the scientific core of this paper: an in-window calibrated `powermetrics` instrument; an attribution-limited finding of roughly 1 J per phase member; LABELLED floors composed from repeatability, worst-case edge placement, and never-zero drift; separate floor-clearance and interval-direction gates; and a fail-closed protocol with pre-registration, admission checks, counterbalancing, hash-bound custody, and published refusals. No claim-bearing numbers currently exist: historical values are diagnostic only. D-117 therefore requires three fresh prospective windows—1.5B decode floor, 7B decode floor, and 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast—with prefill floors riding the first two. Before those nights, the two-slot live-calibration ledger, D-102 successor path, multi-cell mint, frozen plans, extraction specifications, and synthetic regressions must land. Those three approximately 2.8–3.25-hour windows then mint four phase-floor cells and the model-size contrast, after which the existing draft can be populated.
docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-RESULTS_PROSE.md:667:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11254:This paper retains the completed MVP’s scientific spine: `powermetrics` is treated as a calibrated, stack-specific instrument; phase edges are live-bracketed; detection floors combine repeatability, worst-case timing attribution, and never-zero drift; and claims must separately clear the floor and an interval-supported direction gate. The central result remains that the instrument is attribution-limited—roughly 1 J can move across a phase boundary—and practical phase contrasts should be sized around the approximately 5 J effective bar. First complete D-117 exactly as frozen: the 1.5B decode-floor window with prefill rider (~3.14 h), the 7B equivalent (~3.24 h), and the 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast (~2.80 h). Mint the four phase-floor cells, govern the contrast against the two decode floors, and populate the MVP tables. Those three windows contribute the paper’s metrology evidence and Qwen2.5 demonstration; their floors cannot be borrowed for MoE.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-RESULTS_PROSE.md:689:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11456:JouleWise already contains the spine of a strong measurement-methodology paper: a complete-in-structure MVP draft; a 59-pulse, in-window bracket calibration; worst-case phase-edge integration; separately measured repeatability and never-zero drift; two independent claim gates; and a fail-closed, hash-bound protocol whose refusals are retained as evidence. Its central empirical finding is that the M3 Max instrument is attribution-limited: roughly 30 ms of edge uncertainty across a roughly 33 W transition can misassign about 1 J, while ordinary repeatability is nearer 0.3 J. Because the calibrated floor and the contrast’s own interval are separate requirements, practical phase contrasts need roughly 5 J, and repetition cannot average away the boundary term. No current demonstration number is claim-bearing: D-117 therefore requires three fresh prospective windows—1.5B decode floor with a free prefill rider, 7B decode floor with a prefill rider, and a 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast—budgeted at 3.14, 3.24, and 2.80 hours respectively. From today, first finish the two-slot calibration-ledger session, D-102 successor builder, four-cell mint, campaign packs, extraction specifications, and synthetic refusal regression; then collect and mint the two floor windows, collect gamma, and populate the MVP tables. Only afterward should this paper add two compact portability sessions on the desktop rig: one NVML GPU-counter characterization and, if the host exposes a usable package-energy counter, one RAPL characterization. The honest target is therefore **five quiet-device sessions: three already required Mac nights plus two estimated 2–3-hour desktop sessions**. If RAPL capability fails at the desk gate, the paper shrinks to a counter-agnostic framework evaluated on `powermetrics` and NVML, with RAPL described only as a future instantiation—not falsely presented as validated.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-MOE_GATES.md:128:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:9759:This paper retains the completed MVP’s scientific spine: `powermetrics` is treated as a calibrated, stack-specific instrument; phase edges are live-bracketed; detection floors combine repeatability, worst-case timing attribution, and never-zero drift; and claims must separately clear the floor and an interval-supported direction gate. The central result remains that the instrument is attribution-limited—roughly 1 J can move across a phase boundary—and practical phase contrasts should be sized around the approximately 5 J effective bar. First complete D-117 exactly as frozen: the 1.5B decode-floor window with prefill rider (~3.14 h), the 7B equivalent (~3.24 h), and the 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast (~2.80 h). Mint the four phase-floor cells, govern the contrast against the two decode floors, and populate the MVP tables. Those three windows contribute the paper’s metrology evidence and Qwen2.5 demonstration; their floors cannot be borrowed for MoE.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-MOE_GATES.md:786:The MVP is fixed and remains the highest-value use of every immediate desk hour. Its scientific spine is already distinctive: phase attribution is systematically limited, repetitions do not remove that limit, and the instrument publishes what it cannot resolve. Honest cost is **four nights**—3.14 h alpha, 3.24 h beta, 2.80 h gamma, and one 2–4 h Window-C characterization night—plus roughly **2–4 concentrated desk/review weeks** for the open D-117 machinery and postcollection pin closure. I estimate an **80–90% chance that a defensible paper survives**, but only about **55–65% that every desired claim cell and characterization row passes without a refusal**. That distinction is healthy: valid refusals still support the paper. The MVP-review verdict was WEAK only as an overgrown ICPE upgrade, not as the capstone paper itself.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-RUNNER.md:14144:docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Evaluation records its timestamp, expiry, artifact and observed bindings, binding-resolution status, and every triggered re-derivation reason. Horizon expiry, OS build change, power-supply change, calibration identity change, or unresolved current binding makes both family bounds stale and refuses with the registered <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code>. A v1 artifact with an authentic pre-addendum seal but no freshness block is replay-readable only to produce that stale refusal; it is never grandfathered. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \

Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-MINT.md:4034:./docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Evaluation records its timestamp, expiry, artifact and observed bindings, binding-resolution status, and every triggered re-derivation reason. Horizon expiry, OS build change, power-supply change, calibration identity change, or unresolved current binding makes both family bounds stale and refuses with the registered <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code>. A v1 artifact with an authentic pre-addendum seal but no freshness block is replay-readable only to produce that stale refusal; it is never grandfathered. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. The superseded pre-SCREEN+BUDGET gross-only v1 shape (no <code>claim_family_bounds</code>) is not replayable and refuses as malformed/underived; &quot;pre-addendum replay&quot; applies only to the dual-family shape with <code>claim_family_bounds</code> present and freshness absent.</p> <p>The bracket is a WHOLE-WINDOW check: the evaluated basis must contain both endpoints. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \

docs/paper/draft-v1.md:248:**Attribution-limited resolution.** The dominant uncertainty on the studied implementation is boundary placement, not scatter. Roughly one joule per phase member can be misassigned when calibrated timing uncertainty of tens of milliseconds meets a power swing of tens of watts, and repetitions do not reduce it. When attribution dominance is the sole otherwise-refusing condition and an exact corner-widened floor exists, the result may be published with an explicit attribution-limited label; that label never rescues any other refusal. The floor plus claim-side bound remains a practical several-joule sizing disclosure, not one summed acceptance threshold. A historical non-claim diagnostic of the short-prompt model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above that practical bar, but its composed interval overlapped the bar. That diagnostic motivated the prospective floors-only prompt-processing default in Section 7; it was not a fresh measurement or an issued refusal. The resulting limitation concerns what this implementation, on the named stack and boundary, can support.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:258:**Operational constraints as evidence.** Claim-bearing windows require a machine quiescent to the admission gates—no interactive agent sessions, displays asleep, and background work settled. Characterization captures of the idle environment, kept permanently non-claim-bearing, show a low but bursty floor whose excursions, not its mean, threaten a several-joule practical clearance size; idle subtraction cancels only the steady part. The zero-agent window rule is therefore load-bearing, and results collected outside it would not be admitted.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:4817:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11254:This paper retains the completed MVP’s scientific spine: `powermetrics` is treated as a calibrated, stack-specific instrument; phase edges are live-bracketed; detection floors combine repeatability, worst-case timing attribution, and never-zero drift; and claims must separately clear the floor and an interval-supported direction gate. The central result remains that the instrument is attribution-limited—roughly 1 J can move across a phase boundary—and practical phase contrasts should be sized around the approximately 5 J effective bar. First complete D-117 exactly as frozen: the 1.5B decode-floor window with prefill rider (~3.14 h), the 7B equivalent (~3.24 h), and the 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast (~2.80 h). Mint the four phase-floor cells, govern the contrast against the two decode floors, and populate the MVP tables. Those three windows contribute the paper’s metrology evidence and Qwen2.5 demonstration; their floors cannot be borrowed for MoE.
