docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:4948:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11385:The D-117 contrast is low-risk scientifically: the historical diagnostic decode effect is **141.29 J**, roughly 28× the stated 5 J sizing bar and about 10× the historical 7B comparative-floor diagnostic of 14.0 J. Neither historical number is claim-bearing, but both justify the design. The 128-token prefill contrast is excluded: its diagnostic point effect is 5.81 J, but its interval reaches approximately 4.0 J. A refusal would mean “not resolvable at this workload,” not equality.
docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:4995:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11432:The D-117 contrast is low-risk scientifically: the historical diagnostic decode effect is **141.29 J**, roughly 28× the stated 5 J sizing bar and about 10× the historical 7B comparative-floor diagnostic of 14.0 J. Neither historical number is claim-bearing, but both justify the design. The 128-token prefill contrast is excluded: its diagnostic point effect is 5.81 J, but its interval reaches approximately 4.0 J. A refusal would mean “not resolvable at this workload,” not equality.
docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:5019:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11456:JouleWise already contains the spine of a strong measurement-methodology paper: a complete-in-structure MVP draft; a 59-pulse, in-window bracket calibration; worst-case phase-edge integration; separately measured repeatability and never-zero drift; two independent claim gates; and a fail-closed, hash-bound protocol whose refusals are retained as evidence. Its central empirical finding is that the M3 Max instrument is attribution-limited: roughly 30 ms of edge uncertainty across a roughly 33 W transition can misassign about 1 J, while ordinary repeatability is nearer 0.3 J. Because the calibrated floor and the contrast’s own interval are separate requirements, practical phase contrasts need roughly 5 J, and repetition cannot average away the boundary term. No current demonstration number is claim-bearing: D-117 therefore requires three fresh prospective windows—1.5B decode floor with a free prefill rider, 7B decode floor with a prefill rider, and a 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast—budgeted at 3.14, 3.24, and 2.80 hours respectively. From today, first finish the two-slot calibration-ledger session, D-102 successor builder, four-cell mint, campaign packs, extraction specifications, and synthetic refusal regression; then collect and mint the two floor windows, collect gamma, and populate the MVP tables. Only afterward should this paper add two compact portability sessions on the desktop rig: one NVML GPU-counter characterization and, if the host exposes a usable package-energy counter, one RAPL characterization. The honest target is therefore **five quiet-device sessions: three already required Mac nights plus two estimated 2–3-hour desktop sessions**. If RAPL capability fails at the desk gate, the paper shrinks to a counter-agnostic framework evaluated on `powermetrics` and NVML, with RAPL described only as a future instantiation—not falsely presented as validated.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:5285:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md-11722-| Contrast | 1.5B expected Δdecode | 7B expected Δdecode | Versus ~5 J bar |
docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:5368:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11805:JouleWise already has the scientific spine for this paper. The MVP draft defines `powermetrics` as a calibrated, stack-specific instrument; measures phase-boundary attribution with live-bracketed pulse trains; composes repeatability, worst-case timing attribution, and never-zero drift into labelled floors; applies separate floor-clearance and interval-supported-direction gates; and preserves pre-registration, ABBA ordering, custody, and refusals. The instrument is attribution-limited at roughly 1 J per phase member, producing a practical phase-contrast sizing bar near 5 J. No current number is claim-bearing: historical floors and contrasts remain diagnostic after D-110/D-117. D-117 replaces them with three prospective windows: 1.5B decode floor plus prefill rider (budget 3.14 h), 7B decode floor plus rider (3.24 h), and 1.5B-versus-7B decode contrast (2.80 h). Before those nights, the two-slot live-calibration ledger, acceptance-successor machinery, four-cell mint, campaign pinsets, extraction specifications, and synthetic integration regression must land.
docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-plan-factory/DRAFT-QUANT_GATES.md:5461:docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-PRAGMATICS-FIRST.md:11898:**Experiment plan.** Use five simultaneous paired blocks for four active levels: calibration pulse load, 1.5B 128/512, 1.5B 4096/64, and 7B 128/512; reserve one workload family as the held-out bridge test. Include battery-neutralized idle references and ABBA-like order. Historical internal energies span roughly **47 J to ~200 J**, so the workloads themselves are comfortably measurable. The actual wall-minus-SoC residual is unknown and may be **below 5 J**. The existing ~5 J phase-contrast sizing bar does not automatically govern the external meter; a new paired meter/synchronization floor does. A sub-floor residual permits only “no boundary difference resolved,” never equivalence. New capabilities are external trace import, clock alignment, meter metadata, paired reduction, and boundary calibration. Simultaneous telemetry does not alter the single-request boundary.

<p>The guide and complete decision index continue on Archive 1; the navigation on this page links every rendered part.</p> <span id="d-078"></span><h2 id="d-078-soundness-gate-no-claim-bearing-extraction-from-time-anchor-defective-powermetrics-corpora">D-078: Soundness gate — no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-19. Owner: lead session under Ed&#39;s soundness-audit directive; recorded so the gate binds future sessions immediately. Status update 2026-07-22: the gate has been operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the entire repair arc, and Ed explicitly ratified the close-out cap (clause 8); formal ratification of this original text rides the PR #79 review (Ed may amend).</p> <p>The 2026-07-19 measurement-soundness audit (<code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>; all P0 findings lead-verified from primary evidence) found that powermetrics trace timestamps are misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale (pre-spawn/first-parse midpoint anchor), making request/phase/item point energies physically non-attributable as recorded across ALL existing powermetrics corpora, including the 2026-07-17 published floor extraction.</p> <p>Binding until amended:</p> <ol> <li>No claim-bearing floor, MDE, or L2/L3 energy claim may be published from any corpus collected under the defective anchor. Existing corpora are instrument/calibration evidence only.</li> <li>Extraction must treat <code>window_evidence_precheck</code> as a hard gate and must join campaign-log cooldown/admission evidence (cap hits are not clean n). &quot;Claim-eligible&quot; narrative language may describe METRIC-level eligibility only, never source provenance alone.</li> <li>The repair path (roadmap Phase 0, <code>docs/phase_2/splitwise_replication_roadmap.md</code>): tight causal anchor + anchor-shift joule envelope in reduction, analysis-engine 0.5.0/v2 wire compat, CPU-aware idle admission, prospective NEG-8 acceptance threshold. Stored summaries are never rewritten; fixes are prospective.</li> <li>The 2026-07-17 published floor table is caveated in PROJECT_STATUS pending re-extraction; advisor-brief/site correction timing is Ed&#39;s deployment decision (D-068).</li> </ol> <p>Revisit trigger: Phase 0 repair lands with live pulse-validation evidence, or Ed rules a different salvage/disposition for existing corpora.</p> <h3>D-078 amendment — 2026-07-20: fail-closed vocabulary and immutable summaries</h3> <p>Additive amendment under the adversarial soundness fix round. The following spellings are the binding, closed registry for D-078 claim refusals and campaign conditions. Consumers preserve these strings verbatim; an unknown claim/refusal spelling never becomes a pass.</p> <ul> <li>Reducer/analysis claim barriers: <code>nonpositive_window_duration</code>, <code>insufficient_in_window_samples</code>, <code>cadence_ratio_unrecorded</code>, <code>cadence_ratio_below_threshold</code>, <code>clock_bound_unrecorded</code>, <code>anchor_energy_envelope_unrecorded</code>, <code>anchor_energy_envelope_exceeds_quarter_metric</code>, <code>instrument_calibration_missing</code>, <code>instrument_calibration_mismatch</code>, and <code>instrument_calibration_invalid</code>.</li> <li>Floor-extraction refusals: <code>bundle_missing</code>, <code>summary_unreadable</code>, <code>bundle_strict_invalid</code>, <code>bundle_hash_unresolved</code>, <code>bundle_status_not_succeeded</code>, <code>reducer_wire_unknown</code>, <code>idle_method_pair_invalid</code>, <code>metric_missing_or_nonfinite</code>, The claim envelope is now the extrema over start = <code>delta_common + eps_on</code>, stop = <code>delta_common + eps_off</code> with <code>|delta_common| &lt;= B_bundle</code> and <code>|eps_on|, |eps_off| &lt;= B_fiducial</code> independent. For nonnegative power the energy is monotone in each edge separately, so exact extrema are attained at the four edge corners with the common shift scanned continuously — the existing breakpoint-exact scan run per corner. The per-edge corner offset is <code>±(B_fiducial + wall_minus_monotonic_span)</code>: the span is a third disjoint per-edge error source, folded into the corners (delta-review amendment) rather than the frozen arms&#39; cruder <code>2·span·maxP</code> additive term, and the composed <code>anchor_bound_s</code> = <code>B_bundle + B_fiducial + span</code> governs the tail-sufficiency gate identically. Idle-subtracted and per-token envelopes additionally widen by <code>2·(B_fiducial + span)·P_idle</code> because independent edges vary the subtracted idle duration (delta re-audit catch). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

7:     7	Published energy figures for large language model (LLM) inference rarely state the smallest difference their measurement method can trust. This omission matters on consumer hardware, where Apple's *powermetrics* utility estimates processor power without a laboratory meter and where small timing errors can move energy across the boundary between prompt processing and token generation. JouleWise treats the software counter as a scientific instrument. It marks phase boundaries in the runtime, calibrates how far sampled power edges can shift, and combines measured repeatability, worst-case boundary attribution, and drift into a *detection floor*: the smallest difference the method can trust under the stated conditions. Missing, stale, or inconsistent evidence produces a refusal rather than an optimistic result. The main physical finding is that a boundary-timing uncertainty of roughly 30 ms during a power swing of roughly 33 W can move about one joule into the wrong phase; because this is an attribution error rather than random scatter, repetition cannot remove it. Floor clearance and interval-supported direction are therefore enforced as separate gates. When attribution dominance is the sole publication issue, the floor is published with an explicit label naming that limitation. The method is scoped to one named Apple-silicon machine, software stack, and measurement boundary. The demonstration applies the discipline to phase-resolved measurements of two model sizes and will report whether each registered contrast is resolvable or must be refused.
11:    11	Energy numbers for large language model (LLM) inference now appear in leaderboards, systems papers, product comparisons, and policy debates. Published estimates for apparently similar queries can differ by an order of magnitude, yet the numbers are rarely accompanied by an error bar that says how small a difference the measurement method can actually distinguish. This omission is especially consequential on consumer hardware. Apple's *powermetrics* utility makes processor power estimates available without a laboratory meter and is therefore attractive for repeated experiments, but, to our knowledge, it has not been validated in published work as an instrument for separating the energy of LLM inference phases. Apple describes its outputs as estimates; treating them as exact readings can turn timing uncertainty at a phase boundary into a spurious energy difference.
15:    15	We argue that a software power counter should be treated as a scientific instrument rather than as a logging convenience. The instrument must be calibrated in the same session in which it is used; each reported result must carry a detection floor; and the analysis must decline a directional claim when the observed effect cannot pass both the floor and direction gates. JouleWise implements this discipline for phase-resolved, single-request LLM inference on one named Apple-silicon machine and software stack. The runtime emits the phase boundaries because it drives the workload, while *powermetrics* supplies the power samples integrated between those boundaries.
17:    17	This scope is deliberately narrow. A measurement characterizes one physical unit, operating-system build, runtime and library stack, model artifact, quantization, tokenizer, sampling policy, single-request execution policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. It does not establish that an Apple hardware class or vendor is more efficient than another platform. Without an external power meter, absolute values remain internal to the named *powermetrics* system-on-chip boundary; same-boundary contrasts can still be scientifically useful when they pass the calibration and floor gates. Gross joules per request are the primary energy metric. Joules per prompt or output token are tokenizer-scoped companion metrics and are never treated as tokenizer-independent work units.
22:    22	2. Detection floors composed from measured repeatability, worst-case attribution, and measured drift, published with every eligible result.
24:    24	4. A full characterization design for linearity, null response across magnitudes, empirical floor verification, phase-attribution causal consistency, drift and settling, with results pending.
56:    56	The pre- and post-window calibrations form a bracket around the measurements. Both must be authenticated, fresh, and causally outside the science interval. The operative timing bound is the larger of the two calibration bounds plus a never-zero allowance for the drift observed between them: the absolute difference between the pre- and post-window calibrations is screened against a derived bracket-drift limit of about 10.82 ms, and the allowance applied is the larger of the observed difference and that limit, so even a perfectly agreeing bracket carries the full screening allowance. A small repeatability-only excess over the screen is propagated into every floor and claim, while an identified systematic defect cannot be absorbed by that budget. If the post-window bound is larger than the one used when a member was first reduced, the member must be reduced again through the pre-specified path with the wider bound or it cannot support a claim; metadata is never patched to make the bounds agree. A pre-flight level screen also runs before the first science member. It rejects a calibration whose fitted lag is outside the previously characterized family, such as a graphics-processor frequency ramp that the pulse model could mistake for a timing shift. A retry is allowed only after a specific cause is identified and removed, within the retry count frozen before collection. Repeating merely until a favorable calibration appears would be selection on the outcome.
58:    58	This procedure validates timing attribution, not the gain of the power counter. The pulses are graphics-processor matrix multiplications under a relatively light central-processor load, so transfer of their timing bound to sustained mixed-load inference is an explicit assumption. The in-session bracket, empirical floor probes in Section 6, and stack-specific labels constrain that assumption; only an external meter could additionally validate the absolute whole-system scale.
60:    60	## 4. Detection-floor composition
62:    62	A *measurement cell* is one declared family of conditions sharing the telemetry backend, metric, phase or other interval type, workload profile, and stack identity. Its *detection floor* is a practical guard against false observed effects under that family, not a claim that a population percentile has been estimated exactly. JouleWise computes separate absolute and comparative floors and takes their maximum for the cell. An absolute floor measures how far repeated measurements of the same condition wander from their mean. A comparative floor measures the apparent difference between labels that are deliberately made identical and collected in A/B/B/A order.
66:    66	For an absolute cell, \(E_i\) is the energy in joules of the \(i\)th valid bundle, \(\bar E\) is the mean energy, \(r_i=E_i-\bar E\) is its residual, \(s_r\) is the sample standard deviation of those residuals, and \(n\) is the number of valid bundles. The point repeatability guard is
81:    81	so a positive \(\delta_i\) means condition B used more energy than condition A. For \(n\) valid blocks, \(\bar\delta\) is the mean block difference and \(s_\delta\) is its sample standard deviation. The comparative point guard is
85:    85	|\bar\delta|+t_{0.975,n-1}s_\delta\sqrt{1+1/n}\right).
92:    92	Point repeatability is not the full floor. Each energy value is an interval from the timing calibration in Section 3. The floor computation evaluates the complete point-floor estimator over the joint corners of all admitted member intervals, then takes the largest value. For a null ABBA block, the four signed member intervals are propagated through the contrast together. This corner calculation is deliberately conservative: a systematic boundary-placement error is not independent Gaussian noise, so adding it in root-sum-square form would understate the worst case. The published floor is no smaller than the largest accepted attribution width.
107:   107	For each absolute or comparative component, the guarded, corner-widened value is increased once by its matching drift allowance. Let \(F_{\mathrm{abs}}\) and \(F_{\mathrm{cmp}}\) denote those final absolute and comparative energy magnitudes in joules. The operative floor for a cell is
113:   113	where \(F_{\mathrm{cell}}\) is also an energy magnitude in joules. The components are not summed. Cross-window components keep their own calibration basis and allowance; an allowance is never added again at the cell or reporting level. Operative floor values and their full decomposition for each demonstration stack are withheld until corrected artifacts are issued: **[RESULT PENDING CORRECTED ARTIFACTS]**.
117:   117	When timing attribution dominates, a floor may be published with an explicit attribution-limited label only if that dominance is the sole otherwise-refusing condition and an exact corner-widened floor exists. The published result identifies the dominant source as energy uncertainty caused by shifting the phase edges within the calibrated clock-anchor bound. It publishes the corner-widened value rather than the smaller point diagnostic and retains the point-only repeatability value as a diagnostic that cannot support a claim. The label never rescues any other refusal: missing, stale, contaminated, or inconsistent evidence remains terminal.
119:   119	A claim then faces two separate gates, enforced separately. First, the magnitude of its point estimate must exceed \(F_{\mathrm{cell}}\), the cell floor. Second, both endpoints of its fully composed decision interval must support the pre-registered direction. Let \(B_{\mathrm{claim}}\) be the claim-side measurement-uncertainty magnitude in joules carried by that interval. The project also discloses
125:   125	For the measured phase-contrast regime, this practical sizing quantity is several joules. It explains how large an effect will generally need to be to clear both gates together and ensures that neither physical uncertainty term is hidden as an apparent double count. It is not a single summed acceptance threshold, and the decision interval is not compared with the sum. Effects that fail the floor gate are reported as *not resolvable*, not as zero, equal, or evidence of no difference. Effects that pass the floor gate but whose interval does not support direction remain unresolved and receive no directional claim.
135:   135	Prospective sizing is part of that freeze. Before collection, the planned effect, workload, and number of independent bundles or ABBA blocks are compared with the cell floor and the claim-side interval width. If the design has too little expected clearance, the operator must prospectively increase independent evidence, change the workload, or narrow the claim; the choice cannot be made after seeing claim data. A workload change is not merely a sensitivity adjustment. For example, lengthening the prompt changes the population of requests being estimated and therefore changes the estimand itself.
141:   141	Comparisons use the ABBA blocks defined in Section 4. Conditions A and B are measured in the order A, B, B, A, with ordinary cooldown between members. Averaging the two outer A observations and the two inner B observations cancels a linear time trend within the block to first order. For null-floor calibration, A and B are aliases of the same configuration and payload, so any nonzero block difference is a false comparative effect. For scientific contrasts, the A and B definitions are frozen in advance, and the contrast is computed within each block before blocks are aggregated. ABBA reduces common drift; it does not replace the measured whole-window drift allowance.
149:   149	Custody — the requirement that every claim trace back to tamper-evident evidence — continues after collection. The immutable corpus is backed up before extraction. The extractor re-authenticates member hashes, required files and cross-file consistency, calibration identity, environment admission, complete campaign membership, cooldown evidence, phase metric identity, and the whole-window drift allowance. It excludes or refuses a cell according to the frozen rules; missing uncertainty never becomes zero. The present boundary is narrower than an independently reusable floor file: a claim-bearing floor must be produced by protocol-controlled extraction and consumed by analysis in one controlled session run and verified by the experimenters. A standalone floor or result artifact is not independently sufficient to authorize a claim.
151:   151	The refusal log is part of the evaluation, not an embarrassment to omit. It records contaminated members, out-of-family calibration, stale drift evidence, unresolved clock anchors, duplicate recorded occurrences, and below-floor effects. In one real end-of-night case, governed re-evaluation refused a window because a member's internal clock alignment could not be resolved. Independent adjudication found that refusal correct. The result remained non-claim-bearing: an example of the fail-closed design working as intended, not a software defect to be bypassed.
155:   155	The planned instrument characterization will ask whether the complete measurement system behaves predictably when driven by signals whose qualitative answer is known in advance. The workload will serve as a test signal rather than as the scientific finding. Each test will retain the calibration, admission, custody, and floor rules used for the later demonstration. Existing campaign fragments will not be promoted where the governing whole-window verdict did not pass; the table marks every required claim-bearing result as pending.
159:   159	| Linearity | The study will hold the prompt profile fixed and ramp the requested output from 128 to 2048 tokens. It will regress gross request and token-generation energy on the runtime-observed output count and inspect residual structure as well as the fitted slope. | Energy would respond proportionally over the tested dynamic range, and the fitted per-token slope could serve as the known-effect standard for floor probes on this stack. It would not establish linearity outside the tested range or on another stack. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
160:   160	| Null response across magnitudes | The study will run identical A-equals-B ABBA blocks at short, medium, and long output magnitudes and evaluate the paired differences against zero and the predicted decision envelopes. | The comparison path would not create a directional effect merely because total energy or duration changes, and false contrasts across the tested range would be contained by the error model. A non-significant result alone would remain insufficient; the interval must be interpreted relative to the floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
161:   161	| Empirical floor verification | The study will use the pre-registered linearity slope to create micro-differences with predicted effects near 0.5, 1, 1.5, and 3 times the declared floor, in positive and negative counterbalanced blocks. | Sub-floor effects would be refused while sufficiently super-floor effects cleared in both directions. This would test the operational detection boundary, not the counter's absolute gain. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
164:   164	| Between-session stability | The study will repeat calibrations, null blocks, and floor cells across at least three sessions or days with the full stack identity recorded. | The calibration and floor could be reused only under their declared freshness and identity rules, or the study would show that a new session must issue a new floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
176:   176	The planned demonstration will ask a deliberately modest scientific question: on one named consumer stack, how does phase-resolved energy per request differ between two sizes of the same model family, and can each registered difference pass its own floor and direction gates? The two conditions will be instruction-tuned models of the same family at roughly 1.5 and 7 billion parameters, both 4-bit quantized, served by the same runtime with an identical prompt and fixed output budget. Demonstration measurements will be collected in dedicated quiet windows under Section 5, with the floors of Section 4 derived from the protocol-controlled floor windows.
180:   180	Each model size will receive its own floor cell per phase: an absolute-repeatability arm and a null ABBA arm, both frozen before collection. The adopted pre-registered default keeps prompt-processing floor cells in both model-specific floor windows but registers the model-size directional contrast for token generation only. The contrast will be computed within ABBA blocks whose A and B are the two model sizes, on the frozen phase-energy metric. Its floor gate will compare the point-estimate magnitude with the cell floor; its separate direction gate will ask whether both endpoints of the composed interval support the registered direction.
184:   184	A non-claim diagnostic analysis of earlier captures informed that default. For the natural short prompt, the prompt-processing model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above the practical joint-clearance bar, while its composed uncertainty interval overlapped the bar. This was a prospective design warning, not an issued refusal: no fresh demonstration contrast has been measured or refused. The token-generation contrast showed substantially more prospective clearance.
186:   186	One declared alternative remains under consideration and would replace the default only through an operator decision frozen before collection: a longer prompt projected to put the prompt-processing contrast at roughly twice the practical bar. That projection is an extrapolation from prompt-length scaling observed on the smaller model; no long-prompt evidence exists for the larger model, so the fresh arm would be its first direct test. Lengthening the prompt would also change the estimand, as Section 5 explains. All results in this section are reported under the adopted default unless that replacement is frozen first.
194:   194	| Phase | Model | Gross J/request (lower, upper) | J per prompt token | J per output token | Cell floor (labelled) | n |
201:   201	Table 2. The pre-registered contrast and the declared floors-only phase on the same stack. A registered contrast will aggregate independent ABBA blocks. The floor gate compares the point-estimate magnitude with the cell floor; the direction gate checks whether both endpoints of the fully composed interval support the registered direction. The claim-side bound is shown separately. The two gates are not replaced by a summed threshold.
203:   203	| Contrast | Point estimate | Interval [lower, upper] | Cell floor | Clearance (point − floor) | Claim-side bound | Floor-gate outcome | Direction-gate outcome | Verdict |
206:   206	| prompt processing, 7B − 1.5B | not registered under the adopted default | not registered | [PENDING] | not applicable | not applicable | not evaluated | not evaluated | floors only |
208:   208	The narrative will state, for each registered contrast, whether both gates passed and will quote the refusal log where the protocol declined evidence. Joules per token are tokenizer-scoped companion metrics; they will not be compared across tokenizers. A quantization ladder will be included only if it is collected under its own stack-specific floors within the frozen window budget.
216:   216	Prompt length illustrates why feasibility is tied to the estimand. A longer prompt can increase prompt-processing energy and make a contrast easier to resolve, but it answers a different question about a different request population. Feasibility therefore means that a pre-registered design can adjudicate the effect it actually names, not that the workload can be enlarged until any difference becomes visible. Beyond this Apple-silicon stack, the transferable contribution is the method—calibrate boundary attribution, measure drift, separate floor and direction gates, and preserve refusals—not the numerical floor, which must be established again for each instrument, boundary, and stack.

    13	
    14	JouleWise is an extensible measurement harness for energy-wise LLM inference
    15	across heterogeneous local hardware. The benchmark layered on that harness is
    16	the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. The name is a
    17	deliberate nod to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement as the spine,
    18	split inference as the first major research application.
    19	
    20	The harness is designed around three stable ideas:
    21	
    22	- Typed experiment configs define what should run.
    23	- Runtime and telemetry adapters define how each hardware target is exercised
    24	  and measured.
    25	- Run bundles preserve raw traces, events, metadata, logs, and summary metrics
    26	  for later audit and analysis.
    27	
    28	**Status:** research prototype. The Mac (Apple M3 Max) measurement harness has
    29	completed its instrument repair (D-078 phase 0) and the repaired path has
    30	collected 229 strict members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those
    31	windows are non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence, not
    32	published floors. The SCREEN+BUDGET rules are ratified and merged
    33	(D-078 clause 10; council C-045):
    34	they screen gross and idle-subtracted energy separately, retain a nonzero
    35	drift allowance for each family, require a fresh 24-hour bound, reject
    36	fallback-clock members from floor cells, and bar mock evidence from claims.
    37	Five prospective quiet-machine windows have since passed under those rules
    38	(C, D, a10, the 7B floor window, and the contrast window). The first floor
    39	artifact was minted on 2026-07-30, but D-110 has since made that mint
    40	**NON-CLAIM-BEARING until it is re-derived under the repaired calibration
    41	selector**. The Splitwise head-to-head contrast (1.5B vs 7B decode) has been
    42	collected and passed its collection and whole-window verdict gates; its
    43	bookkeeping machinery and generalized mint tooling are mainline, but D-110
    44	blocks claim use and the next floor mint until the ruled repair and remint
    45	conditions are satisfied. The a8 re-verdict path is closed. The
    46	project's framing is now metrology-centric (D-091): the measurement
    47	instrument itself is the product, and model comparisons are demonstrations
    48	of what it can resolve.
    49	
    50	The post-audit architectural verdicts remain deliberately bounded: AXI-SB is
    51	`supported` for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped
    52	observability, while AXI-SC is `unsupported_for_joulewise` on the pinned
    53	runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution
    54	surface is absent. Neither is energy evidence. This summary does not select
    55	work: the generated state-kernel regions in `RUN_STATE.md` and `TASK_QUEUE.md`

     4	model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it

     6	decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review
     7	reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise —
     8	positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.

     1	# JouleWise: Attribution-Limited Detection Floors for Phase-Resolved LLM Inference Energy on Apple Silicon
     2	
     3	*Draft: demonstration values, instrument-characterization results, and archive locators are pending; bracketed markers show where they will land.*
     4	
     5	## Abstract
     6	
     7	Published energy figures for large language model (LLM) inference rarely state the smallest difference their measurement method can trust. This omission matters on consumer hardware, where Apple's *powermetrics* utility estimates processor power without a laboratory meter and where small timing errors can move energy across the boundary between prompt processing and token generation. JouleWise treats the software counter as a scientific instrument. It marks phase boundaries in the runtime, calibrates how far sampled power edges can shift, and combines measured repeatability, worst-case boundary attribution, and drift into a *detection floor*: the smallest difference the method can trust under the stated conditions. Missing, stale, or inconsistent evidence produces a refusal rather than an optimistic result. The main physical finding is that a boundary-timing uncertainty of roughly 30 ms during a power swing of roughly 33 W can move about one joule into the wrong phase; because this is an attribution error rather than random scatter, repetition cannot remove it. Floor clearance and interval-supported direction are therefore enforced as separate gates. When attribution dominance is the sole publication issue, the floor is published with an explicit label naming that limitation. The method is scoped to one named Apple-silicon machine, software stack, and measurement boundary. The demonstration applies the discipline to phase-resolved measurements of two model sizes and will report whether each registered contrast is resolvable or must be refused.
     8	
     9	## 1. Introduction
    10	
    11	Energy numbers for large language model (LLM) inference now appear in leaderboards, systems papers, product comparisons, and policy debates. Published estimates for apparently similar queries can differ by an order of magnitude, yet the numbers are rarely accompanied by an error bar that says how small a difference the measurement method can actually distinguish. This omission is especially consequential on consumer hardware. Apple's *powermetrics* utility makes processor power estimates available without a laboratory meter and is therefore attractive for repeated experiments, but, to our knowledge, it has not been validated in published work as an instrument for separating the energy of LLM inference phases. Apple describes its outputs as estimates; treating them as exact readings can turn timing uncertainty at a phase boundary into a spurious energy difference.
    12	
    13	The core difficulty is physical as much as statistical. Energy is the integral of power over time. An experiment may repeat consistently and still assign energy to the wrong phase if a power sample near the boundary between prompt processing and token generation is placed on the wrong side. Averaging more repetitions reduces random scatter but does not remove that attribution error. Slow changes in thermal or background state can add a second false difference over a long collection session.
    14	
    15	We argue that a software power counter should be treated as a scientific instrument rather than as a logging convenience. The instrument must be calibrated in the same session in which it is used; each reported result must carry a detection floor; and the analysis must decline a directional claim when the observed effect cannot pass both the floor and direction gates. JouleWise implements this discipline for phase-resolved, single-request LLM inference on one named Apple-silicon machine and software stack. The runtime emits the phase boundaries because it drives the workload, while *powermetrics* supplies the power samples integrated between those boundaries.
    16	
    17	This scope is deliberately narrow. A measurement characterizes one physical unit, operating-system build, runtime and library stack, model artifact, quantization, tokenizer, sampling policy, single-request execution policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. It does not establish that an Apple hardware class or vendor is more efficient than another platform. Without an external power meter, absolute values remain internal to the named *powermetrics* system-on-chip boundary; same-boundary contrasts can still be scientifically useful when they pass the calibration and floor gates. Gross joules per request are the primary energy metric. Joules per prompt or output token are tokenizer-scoped companion metrics and are never treated as tokenizer-independent work units.
    18	
   150	
   151	The refusal log is part of the evaluation, not an embarrassment to omit. It records contaminated members, out-of-family calibration, stale drift evidence, unresolved clock anchors, duplicate recorded occurrences, and below-floor effects. In one real end-of-night case, governed re-evaluation refused a window because a member's internal clock alignment could not be resolved. Independent adjudication found that refusal correct. The result remained non-claim-bearing: an example of the fail-closed design working as intended, not a software defect to be bypassed.
   152	
   153	## 6. Instrument characterization
   154	
   155	The planned instrument characterization will ask whether the complete measurement system behaves predictably when driven by signals whose qualitative answer is known in advance. The workload will serve as a test signal rather than as the scientific finding. Each test will retain the calibration, admission, custody, and floor rules used for the later demonstration. Existing campaign fragments will not be promoted where the governing whole-window verdict did not pass; the table marks every required claim-bearing result as pending.
   156	
   157	| Property | Planned characterization method | What a passing result would establish | Claim-bearing result |
   158	|---|---|---|---|
   159	| Linearity | The study will hold the prompt profile fixed and ramp the requested output from 128 to 2048 tokens. It will regress gross request and token-generation energy on the runtime-observed output count and inspect residual structure as well as the fitted slope. | Energy would respond proportionally over the tested dynamic range, and the fitted per-token slope could serve as the known-effect standard for floor probes on this stack. It would not establish linearity outside the tested range or on another stack. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
   160	| Null response across magnitudes | The study will run identical A-equals-B ABBA blocks at short, medium, and long output magnitudes and evaluate the paired differences against zero and the predicted decision envelopes. | The comparison path would not create a directional effect merely because total energy or duration changes, and false contrasts across the tested range would be contained by the error model. A non-significant result alone would remain insufficient; the interval must be interpreted relative to the floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
   161	| Empirical floor verification | The study will use the pre-registered linearity slope to create micro-differences with predicted effects near 0.5, 1, 1.5, and 3 times the declared floor, in positive and negative counterbalanced blocks. | Sub-floor effects would be refused while sufficiently super-floor effects cleared in both directions. This would test the operational detection boundary, not the counter's absolute gain. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
   162	| Phase-attribution causal consistency | The study will compare the sum of separately integrated phase energies with the gross energy over their enclosing request. It will then vary output length while holding prompt tokens fixed and fit the slope of prompt-processing energy against output length. | Phase accounting would be additive within its stated boundaries, and energy assigned to prompt processing would not acquire a systematic dependence on work occurring later in token generation. Together these tests would challenge both missing energy and cross-phase leakage. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
   163	| Drift and settling | The study will place long controlled holds and fixed reference workloads through the window, including start, midpoint, and end references. After operator or stage activity, it will repeat the reference while recording the time required for thermal and admission observables to stabilize and compare it with the 180 s operating convention. | The measured drift trajectory would be contained by the published allowance, and the chosen settling time would be supported or revised from observed recovery rather than convenience. Endpoint agreement alone would not be enough if the midpoint revealed curvature. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
   164	| Between-session stability | The study will repeat calibrations, null blocks, and floor cells across at least three sessions or days with the full stack identity recorded. | The calibration and floor could be reused only under their declared freshness and identity rules, or the study would show that a new session must issue a new floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
   165	
   166	Linearity and the null ladder will test complementary failure modes. A smooth response can still carry an offset, and a zero-centered null can coexist with a nonlinear scale. The micro-difference experiment will then close the loop by using the measured slope to place effects deliberately below and above the declared decision boundary. Success will require the instrument to refuse the former and resolve the latter in both directions; merely observing larger effects with larger workloads will not be sufficient.
   167	
   168	The causal tests will address the most important phase-specific risk. Additivity will check conservation inside the declared request boundary: phase intervals should reconcile with the enclosing total, subject to explicitly labelled setup or gap intervals. Causal invariance will check direction: holding the prompt fixed while increasing later token-generation work should not change energy attributed to earlier prompt processing. A nonzero prompt-processing slope would indicate boundary leakage, shared-state coupling that invalidates the simple phase model, or both; it would narrow the claim rather than be explained away.
   169	
   170	Temporal characterization will separate slow drift from thermal settling. Start, midpoint, and end references will expose whole-window curvature, while post-transition references will estimate how long the system takes to return to its admitted state after operator activity or stage churn. Repetition across days will test whether one session's calibration is representative under identical recorded bindings. Internal channel-sum versus package reconciliation will remain a secondary consistency check. External wall-power regression remains conditional on a suitable meter and would validate totals only; the pulse experiment remains the evidence for phase splitting.
   171	
   172	Every resulting figure and table will identify the physical unit, operating-system version and build, runtime and relevant library versions, model artifact hash, quantization, tokenizer identity, sampler and output policy, configured and realized batch or concurrency policy, measurement boundary, and telemetry backend. Measurements will support stack-specific conclusions only; independent replication or a calibrated boundary bridge would be required for hardware-class, vendor-class, or cross-boundary rankings.
   173	
   174	## 7. Demonstration results
   175	
   176	The planned demonstration will ask a deliberately modest scientific question: on one named consumer stack, how does phase-resolved energy per request differ between two sizes of the same model family, and can each registered difference pass its own floor and direction gates? The two conditions will be instruction-tuned models of the same family at roughly 1.5 and 7 billion parameters, both 4-bit quantized, served by the same runtime with an identical prompt and fixed output budget. Demonstration measurements will be collected in dedicated quiet windows under Section 5, with the floors of Section 4 derived from the protocol-controlled floor windows.
   177	
   178	### Pre-registered design
   179	
   180	Each model size will receive its own floor cell per phase: an absolute-repeatability arm and a null ABBA arm, both frozen before collection. The adopted pre-registered default keeps prompt-processing floor cells in both model-specific floor windows but registers the model-size directional contrast for token generation only. The contrast will be computed within ABBA blocks whose A and B are the two model sizes, on the frozen phase-energy metric. Its floor gate will compare the point-estimate magnitude with the cell floor; its separate direction gate will ask whether both endpoints of the composed interval support the registered direction.
   181	
   182	### Prospective workload sizing
   183	
   184	A non-claim diagnostic analysis of earlier captures informed that default. For the natural short prompt, the prompt-processing model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above the practical joint-clearance bar, while its composed uncertainty interval overlapped the bar. This was a prospective design warning, not an issued refusal: no fresh demonstration contrast has been measured or refused. The token-generation contrast showed substantially more prospective clearance.
   185	
   186	One declared alternative remains under consideration and would replace the default only through an operator decision frozen before collection: a longer prompt projected to put the prompt-processing contrast at roughly twice the practical bar. That projection is an extrapolation from prompt-length scaling observed on the smaller model; no long-prompt evidence exists for the larger model, so the fresh arm would be its first direct test. Lengthening the prompt would also change the estimand, as Section 5 explains. All results in this section are reported under the adopted default unless that replacement is frozen first.
   187	
   188	### Results
   189	
   190	**[RESULT PENDING CORRECTED ARTIFACTS — tables below are structural placeholders; no energy value from superseded artifacts is carried into this draft.]**
   191	
   192	Table 1. Phase results on the studied stack. The caption accompanying populated results will state the common physical unit, operating system, runtime and libraries, model artifact and quantization, tokenizer, sampler and output policy, concurrency policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. Each interval will be the fully composed two-sided measurement interval; \(n\) counts independent valid run bundles, not samples or items within a bundle.
   236	Prospective paired minimum-detectable-effect methods estimate the smallest effect a planned paired study has adequate statistical power to find. They size a study from paired variation and can impose a one-way prior ratchet: observed variability may raise the planned threshold but may not lower it after outcomes are seen [12]. JouleWise uses that logic for prospective design, but it does not treat the worst-case attribution term as independent random noise. Root-sum-square composition would be anti-conservative for a systematic edge-placement bound. Instead, the analysis maximizes over calibrated edge positions, measures drift with bracketed references, and publishes the resulting floor with the effect.
   237	
   238	This emphasis changes the role of failed runs. A rejected admission, stale calibration, contaminated member, or below-floor contrast is evidence about the instrument's operating domain. Hash-bound raw traces, runtime events, configurations, supersessions, verdicts, and pre-registration records make that evidence capable of being reduced again under the governed process. The refusal is retained rather than disappearing behind a final average.
   239	
   240	### Split and disaggregated inference
   241	
   242	Split, or disaggregated, inference places prompt processing and token generation on different devices and transfers intermediate state between them. Revisiting Disaggregated Large Language Model Serving reports essentially unconditionally higher energy for disaggregation on its evaluated two-graphics-processor node, while its performance benefits depend on load, baseline, and transfer conditions [13]. Its energy boundary combines several software telemetry sources into whole-run energy per token. DualScale studies phase placement and per-phase power control but reports graphics-processor-only energy from homogeneous server hardware [14]. Prima.cpp includes whole-run energy and communication accounting but not a per-stage energy split [15], while SplitZip characterizes lossless transfer compression without making an energy claim [16].
   243	
   244	JouleWise does not claim a new split scheduler in this paper. Split inference is instead a demanding future demonstration of the instrument because it introduces two physical boundaries, a transfer interval, and clock alignment across devices. A valid comparison would have to measure both ends, name each boundary, and pass a pre-registered floor or calibrated bridge. Whether splitting saves energy remains an empirical outcome; the reusable contribution is a method that can issue, qualify, or refuse the result.
   245	
   246	## 10. Limitations
   247	
   248	**Attribution-limited resolution.** The dominant uncertainty on the studied implementation is boundary placement, not scatter. Roughly one joule per phase member can be misassigned when calibrated timing uncertainty of tens of milliseconds meets a power swing of tens of watts, and repetitions do not reduce it. When attribution dominance is the sole otherwise-refusing condition and an exact corner-widened floor exists, the result may be published with an explicit attribution-limited label; that label never rescues any other refusal. The floor plus claim-side bound remains a practical several-joule sizing disclosure, not one summed acceptance threshold. A historical non-claim diagnostic of the short-prompt model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above that practical bar, but its composed interval overlapped the bar. That diagnostic motivated the prospective floors-only prompt-processing default in Section 7; it was not a fresh measurement or an issued refusal. The resulting limitation concerns what this implementation, on the named stack and boundary, can support.
   249	
   250	**One unit, one stack, one boundary.** Every result is scoped to one physical machine, operating-system build, runtime and library stack, model artifact, quantization, tokenizer, sampling and output policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. Nothing here ranks hardware classes or vendors, and the whole-system-on-chip boundary of *powermetrics* is not comparable to a graphics-board or wall boundary without a calibrated bridge.
   251	
   252	**No external meter.** The calibration validates timing attribution—whether samples near a commanded edge land inside or outside a phase integral. It does not validate the counter's absolute gain or whole-system scale; absolute joule values remain internal to the named software boundary. A wall-power instrument could test totals but would still not adjudicate the division of a total between phases, which is the question the pulse-train experiment answers.
   253	
   254	**Transfer assumptions.** The calibration pulses are graphics-processor matrix multiplications under light central-processor load; transferring their timing bound to sustained mixed-load inference is an explicit assumption, constrained by the in-window bracket and the planned empirical floor probes but not eliminated. The drift allowance is measured per window with no duration-scaling law because the evidence does not identify one; longer windows than those characterized would need fresh drift evidence.

   121	## Desk recommendation
   122	
   123	**VERDICT: MARGINAL.**
   124	
   125	At the historically measured workload—Qwen2.5 1.5B versus 7B, identical 128-token prompt and 512-token fixed output—the best ABBA estimate is a 7B−1.5B prefill delta of **5.809930 J**. The decision-log practical bar is only approximately **5 J**, leaving **0.809930 J**, or about **16%**, of point-estimate headroom.
   126	
   127	That is not enough to recommend adding the contrast at its existing 128-token shape. The default fork should therefore be:
   128	
   129	- claim prefill floors;
   130	- retain the model contrast as decode-only;
   131	- describe the 128-token prefill contrast as infeasible-to-clear-with-comfort in limitations.
   132	
   133	A prospectively frozen 256-token prompt could change the answer: proportional sensitivity gives approximately **11.619860 J**, comfortably above the approximate bar. Because no historical 7B corpus above 128 prompt tokens exists, that is a sizing projection, not demonstrated evidence.

   176	The planned demonstration will ask a deliberately modest scientific question: on one named consumer stack, how does phase-resolved energy per request differ between two sizes of the same model family, and can each registered difference pass its own floor and direction gates? The two conditions will be instruction-tuned models of the same family at roughly 1.5 and 7 billion parameters, both 4-bit quantized, served by the same runtime with an identical prompt and fixed output budget. Demonstration measurements will be collected in dedicated quiet windows under Section 5, with the floors of Section 4 derived from the protocol-controlled floor windows.
   177	
   178	### Pre-registered design
   179	
   180	Each model size will receive its own floor cell per phase: an absolute-repeatability arm and a null ABBA arm, both frozen before collection. The adopted pre-registered default keeps prompt-processing floor cells in both model-specific floor windows but registers the model-size directional contrast for token generation only. The contrast will be computed within ABBA blocks whose A and B are the two model sizes, on the frozen phase-energy metric. Its floor gate will compare the point-estimate magnitude with the cell floor; its separate direction gate will ask whether both endpoints of the composed interval support the registered direction.
   181	
   182	### Prospective workload sizing
   183	
   184	A non-claim diagnostic analysis of earlier captures informed that default. For the natural short prompt, the prompt-processing model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above the practical joint-clearance bar, while its composed uncertainty interval overlapped the bar. This was a prospective design warning, not an issued refusal: no fresh demonstration contrast has been measured or refused. The token-generation contrast showed substantially more prospective clearance.
   185	
   186	One declared alternative remains under consideration and would replace the default only through an operator decision frozen before collection: a longer prompt projected to put the prompt-processing contrast at roughly twice the practical bar. That projection is an extrapolation from prompt-length scaling observed on the smaller model; no long-prompt evidence exists for the larger model, so the fresh arm would be its first direct test. Lengthening the prompt would also change the estimand, as Section 5 explains. All results in this section are reported under the adopted default unless that replacement is frozen first.

The adopted pre-registered default keeps prompt-processing floor cells in both model-specific floor windows but registers the model-size directional contrast for token generation only.    182	### Prospective workload sizing
   183	
   184	A non-claim diagnostic analysis of earlier captures informed that default. For the natural short prompt, the prompt-processing model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above the practical joint-clearance bar, while its composed uncertainty interval overlapped the bar. This was a prospective design warning, not an issued refusal: no fresh demonstration contrast has been measured or refused. The token-generation contrast showed substantially more prospective clearance.
   185	
   186	One declared alternative remains under consideration and would replace the default only through an operator decision frozen before collection: a longer prompt projected to put the prompt-processing contrast at roughly twice the practical bar. That projection is an extrapolation from prompt-length scaling observed on the smaller model; no long-prompt evidence exists for the larger model, so the fresh arm would be its first direct test. Lengthening the prompt would also change the estimand, as Section 5 explains. All results in this section are reported under the adopted default unless that replacement is frozen first.
   187	
   188	### Results

   246	## 10. Limitations
   247	
   248	**Attribution-limited resolution.** The dominant uncertainty on the studied implementation is boundary placement, not scatter. Roughly one joule per phase member can be misassigned when calibrated timing uncertainty of tens of milliseconds meets a power swing of tens of watts, and repetitions do not reduce it. When attribution dominance is the sole otherwise-refusing condition and an exact corner-widened floor exists, the result may be published with an explicit attribution-limited label; that label never rescues any other refusal. The floor plus claim-side bound remains a practical several-joule sizing disclosure, not one summed acceptance threshold. A historical non-claim diagnostic of the short-prompt model-size contrast had a point estimate marginally above that practical bar, but its composed interval overlapped the bar. That diagnostic motivated the prospective floors-only prompt-processing default in Section 7; it was not a fresh measurement or an issued refusal. The resulting limitation concerns what this implementation, on the named stack and boundary, can support.
   249	
   250	**One unit, one stack, one boundary.** Every result is scoped to one physical machine, operating-system build, runtime and library stack, model artifact, quantization, tokenizer, sampling and output policy, telemetry backend, and measurement boundary. Nothing here ranks hardware classes or vendors, and the whole-system-on-chip boundary of *powermetrics* is not comparable to a graphics-board or wall boundary without a calibrated bridge.
